project_tracker_diagnostic: Tall colony-forming goldenrod with plume-like panicles of many small yellow heads and rougher leaves/stems; often more robust than Canada goldenrod.

project_inclusion.learning_reason: Common or useful Central Texas fall/white composite for field learning.

morphology_keys.habit: Tall erect herb often forming colonies.
morphology_keys.heads: Many very small yellow heads in arching or plume-like panicles.
best_field_traits: If working below species level, do not assign a subspecies from general goldenrod habit alone; Joey's exact reference is S. altissima subsp. gilvocanescens.
morphology_keys.joey_reference_note: Joey's exact iNaturalist photo reference is Solidago altissima subsp. gilvocanescens. Use it as an infraspecific habit/morphology comparison, not as evidence that every local tall goldenrod belongs to that subspecies.

photo_strategy.selection_logic: Prefer curated taxon photos plus multiple views from one Central Texas/Texas observation.

look_here_first: For TALL goldenrod, inspect SHORT, FINE hairs low on a standing stem and a FIRM, often noticeably rough three-nerved middle leaf. Check if upper-mid leaves are entire or sparsely toothed. Compare Canada goldenrod: often thinner more serrated leaves and less crowded longer stem hairs — many characters overlap. Giant goldenrod tends to have genuinely smooth/waxy lower stem. Photograph the stem at ground level and the leaf UNDERSIDE, not only the yellow plume.

photo_diagnostic_lesson.pair: Solidago altissima vs canadensis vs gigantea
photo_diagnostic_lesson.look_here_first: Check lower stem hair texture and an underside leaf before looking at the plume. Giant goldenrod usually smooth below; Altissima dense short stem hairs and firmer rough leaves; Canadensis often more noticeable teeth and somewhat sparser stem hairs.

key.altissima: Typically many short fine hairs, sometimes base less hairy
key.canadensis: Often sparser, longer hairs, base may be smooth
key.gigantea: Usually largely glabrous, sometimes glaucous white waxy cast
key.why: Best starting shot, but not a perfect one-character key

key.altissima: 3 veins; firm blade, upper/mid edges often fewer/smaller teeth
key.canadensis: 3 veins; generally finer more conspicuous serrations
key.gigantea: 3 veins too, narrow blade, often more glabrous
key.why: Need whole leaf and scale; many variants overlap

key.altissima: Often coarse/fine hairs on veins AND between
key.canadensis: Hairs more concentrated on veins but variable
key.why: Supporting trait, don't claim ironclad distinction

key.altissima: Often somewhat larger phyllaries/heads than canadensis
key.why: Measure with 1mm rule when altissima/canadensis still unsure

key.canadensis: Old fields and mesic open habitats

photo_diagnostic_lesson.memory_rule: GIANT = generally SMOOTH stem; TALL = SHORTHAIR firm leaf; CANADA = finer teeth, hair variable. For TALL vs CANADA, examine a bundle of traits.
photo_diagnostic_lesson.caution: Goldenrods of the canadensis–altissima–gigantea complex hybridize/overlap in photos; retain genus-level ID when evidence insufficient.
